title: Expectation of the last-coordinate half-difference
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$, write $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$ for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and set $d(x)=\tfrac12(f_0(x)-f_1(x))$. With expectation taken uniformly over the Boolean cube, $\mathbb E[d]=\tfrac12(\mathbb E[f_0]-\mathbb E[f_1])$.
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, and $d=(f_0-f_1)/2$. Uniform expectation satisfies $\mathbb E d=(\mathbb E f_0-\mathbb E f_1)/2$.
